newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore and Argentine sign air service pact.
newsitem.headline: Singapore and Argentine sign air service pact.

text.p: Singapore and Argentina signed an air service agreement on Thursday to allow for flights between the two countries, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) said.

It said in a statement the new agreement provided the basic framework for Singapore and Argentina to operate three weekly services each between the countries. There are currently no direct flights between them.
Asked when flights wwould begin, a CAAS spokeswoman said "as soon as we can obtain the necessary traffic rights from intermediate countries", because the long flight would require stopovers.
The agreement was signed by Singapore's Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan and Argentina's Minister for Foreign Affairs, International Trade and Worship, Guido di Tella.
The signing was held in conjunction with Argentine President Carlos Menem's visit to Singapore on Thursday, the final leg of a three country tour of Southeast Asia.
